items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I got to work with Sonny Greer there.

ctx.x: Okay. Let me get back to your bio a bit. Was it, the Benny Goodman association, did it take some getting used to with Benny?

Well what happened was I went to Manhattan School of Music in 1976. Music theory major, piano minor. And eventually switched to saxophone major, which means that I got to study with Joe Allard, who was a great teacher, a guy named Dave Tofani, but at the same time, Manhattan School of Music is in the old Juilliard building. It’s up at 122nd Street and Claremont Avenue in Manhattan. And just down the street from where I was living was a club called the West End that was run by Phil Schaap. And this is a major…

Wilder. In other words classically trained, read flyspecks, and even more than Joe, he was different than Joe, he was not the soloist, the great personal soloist that Joe was. He played great, fine solos. But he was like a Snooky Young or Al Killian or he was like a dynamite lead player. And he had a band with Eddie Durham. And I was so desperate to sit in with him I just took out my saxophone one night and, during a break, to show them like that I wasn’t going to muck it up, and I played a little and they said…
